lines.text: The first transistor wore gold foil.
John Bardeen and Walter Brattain worked at Bell Labs in 1947.
lines.say: John Bardeen and Walter Brattain worked at Bell Labs in nineteen forty seven.

lines.text: They were looking for a solid state amplifier.
Their device was a thumb sized slab of germanium.
Brattain put gold foil on the point of a plastic triangle.
He sliced the foil at the tip to make two gold contacts.
The two contacts sat about a sheet of paper's width apart.
A spring pressed the gold tipped wedge against the germanium.
On December 16, 1947, it worked as an amplifier.
lines.say: On December sixteenth, nineteen forty seven, it worked as an amplifier.

lines.text: In 1956, the three men shared the Nobel Prize in Physics.
lines.say: In nineteen fifty six, the three men shared the Nobel Prize in Physics.

post.caption: The first transistor wore gold foil. In 1947, John Bardeen and Walter Brattain worked at Bell Labs, looking for a solid state amplifier. Their device was a thumb sized slab of germanium. Brattain put gold foil on the point of a plastic triangle and sliced the foil at the tip to make two gold contacts, about a sheet of paper's width apart. A spring pressed the wedge against the germanium. On December 16, 1947, it worked as an amplifier. In 1956, the three men shared the Nobel Prize in Physics.
